from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: The Two Pillars", [
            "Differentiation measures the slope of a curve.", 
            "Integration calculates the total area under a curve.", 
            "Velocity is the derivative of position."
        ])
        
        # Create elements
        derivative_pillar = Rectangle(height=2, width=1.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        integral_pillar = Rectangle(height=2, width=1.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        
        d_label = Text("Rate", font_size=24)
        i_label = Text("Accumulation", font_size=24)
        
        self.place_at_grid(derivative_pillar, 'C2')
        self.place_at_grid(integral_pillar, 'C5')
        self.place_at_grid(d_label, 'C2')
        self.place_at_grid(i_label, 'C5')
        
        conn_line = Line(derivative_pillar.get_right(), integral_pillar.get_left(), color=WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(derivative_pillar), FadeIn(d_label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00") # Highlight yellow

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(integral_pillar), FadeIn(i_label))
        self.play(Create(conn_line))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF") # Highlight blue

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            derivative_pillar.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            integral_pillar.animate.set_color("#00FFFF")
        )
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF") # Highlight magenta
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Conceptual Link: Accumulation Functions", 
                          ["Define an accumulation function: A(x).", 
                           "A(x) represents the area under f(t).", 
                           "A(x) is the integral from a to x."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display accumulation function F(x) = ∫ f(t)dt
        eq = MathTex("A(x) = \\int_{a}^{x} f(t) dt", color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(eq, 'B3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(eq))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate area under curve f(t) growing as x moves right
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 3, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda t: 0.5 * (t - 2)**2 + 1, color=WHITE)
        x_tracker = ValueTracker(0.1)
        area = always_redraw(lambda: axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, x_tracker.get_value()], color="#00FF00", opacity=0.5))
        
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'C2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(axes, curve, area)
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(3), run_time=3)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Label the instantaneous height of area as f(x)
        f_label = MathTex("f(x)", color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(f_label, 'C5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(f_label))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF0000")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lines = ["The derivative of area is the height.", "This reveals the inverse relationship of calculus.", "Differentiation cancels out the accumulation.", "The area changes at rate f(x).", "Calculus connects local slopes to total area."]
        self.setup_layout("The Fundamental Theorem (Part 1)", lines)
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 3, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).scale(0.5)
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * x**2 + 1, color=BLUE)
        label = MathTex("f(x)").next_to(curve, UP)
        plot_group = VGroup(axes, curve, label)
        
        self.place_at_grid(plot_group, 'C2', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        formula = MathTex(r"\frac{d}{dx} \int_a^x f(t) dt = f(x)", color=WHITE).scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B5')
        self.play(Write(formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        x_val = 2.5
        rect = axes.get_riemann_rectangles(curve, x_range=[x_val, x_val+0.2], dx=0.2, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.add(rect)
        self.play(Create(rect))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Definite integrals measure total net change.",
            "F(b) minus F(a) yields the integral.",
            "The antiderivative evaluates definite integrals directly.",
            "This simplifies calculating complex areas.",
            "It bridges derivatives with integral values."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Fundamental Theorem (Part 2)", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        formula = MathTex(r"\int_{a}^{b} f(x) \, dx = F(b) - F(a)")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "C3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Colors: Use hex codes as per B001
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # Highlight F(b) and F(a) - B001/B038
        self.play(formula.animate.set_color_by_tex("F(b)", "#00FFFF"),
                  formula.animate.set_color_by_tex("F(a)", "#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFA500"))
        self.wait(2)

            "They complete the mathematical bridge."
        ])

outline.topic: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus: The Bridge Between Slopes and Areas

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Two Pillars
sections.content: Briefly revisit differentiation as finding the slope (velocity) and integration as finding the area (total distance). Use a graphical animation showing a car's speedometer vs. odometer.
sections.example: A delivery drone's velocity curve vs. its cumulative distance traveled.

sections.title: The Conceptual Link: Accumulation Functions
sections.content: Introduce the area function A(x) = ∫[a to x] f(t) dt. Visualize this as a 'sliding curtain' moving across a graph, covering area as 'x' increases.
sections.example: A squirrel gathering nuts: The rate of gathering (nuts/minute) integrated over time gives the total nut pile size.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem (Part 1): The Inverse Relationship
sections.content: Explain that the derivative of the accumulation function is the original function: d/dx [∫[a to x] f(t) dt] = f(x). Graphically demonstrate that the tiny change in area is just a narrow rectangular strip of height f(x).
sections.example: If the rate of water flow into a tank is f(t), the rate of change of the tank's volume is exactly the current flow rate.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem (Part 2): Evaluating Definite Integrals
sections.content: Define the relationship: ∫[a to b] f(x) dx = F(b) - F(a), where F is the antiderivative. This connects the 'net change' to the 'anti-slope'.
sections.example: A rocket's position at time 'b' minus its position at time 'a' equals the integral of its velocity function between those times.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
sections.content: Conclude that differentiation and integration are reverse processes (inverse operations). Display a circular animation showing the transition from f(x) to F(x) and back.
sections.example: A game character: Differentiation takes you from position to velocity; Integration takes you from velocity back to position.
